correctness.rationale: The edge graph is two K_{2d} minus opposite-vertex matchings plus 2d vertical edges. For a generic section, an edge crosses iff its endpoint signs differ. Within a cross-polytope level exactly min(s,2d-s) omitted antipodal edges cross, proving g_d. Vertical monotonicity yields k>=ell and exactly k-ell crossings. Explicit four-case integer-threshold constructions realize all k,ell, and the piecewise completed-square inequalities give the sharp bound and unique equality count-pair. H*=2 sum_{i>=2} x_i+z=0 realizes it. De Loera et al. Lemma 2.1 justifies the nongeneric reduction. Independently reconstructed exact-integer graphs and all 518 pair constructions in d=2..8 plus 18962 functional tests, and brute MAXCUT d=2..4. Infinite validity rests on the proof, not finite tests.

evidence: De Loera et al., arXiv:2412.12419, Theorem 1.1: general maximum floor(n^2/4) for n-vertex polytopes in ambient dimension >3; for our n=4d this reads 4d^2, strictly weaker than 2d(d-1)+2.
Khovanskii (2006), Theorem 7.2 and related estimates concern h-vectors of generic sections of simple polytopes. The cross-polytope prism is nonsimple for d>=3.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General upper bounds and general polytope-slice algorithms do not entail the sharp product-family formula. Khovanskii’s simple-polytope assumptions do not hold for the prisms in dimension >=4.

evidence: The 2026 prism slab reduction provides a useful premise but no bound optimizing antipodal sign splits; the present counting identity g_d(k)+g_d(l)+k-l and maximizing pair are additional steps.
The 2024 perturbation lemma proves reduction to generic sections, not a particular sharp bound.
Khovanskii 2006 treats a different extremal quantity and general h-vector relations.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No inspected statement logically implies the exact maximum, exhaustive generic spectrum and realizability without carrying out new graph and sign-threshold analysis. The perturbation lemma is cited as a borrowed step; no novelty is assigned to it.

evidence: Birkemeyer et al. (arxiv:2609.16195), Proposition 3.6: a prism slice is combinatorially a slab of its base or a prism over a base slice; the displayed proposition makes no cross-polytope cut enumeration.
Khovanskii (2006), PDF p.3 Example 1 describes mean face degrees for a polygonal prism, not this extremal section statistic.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A prism section can be encoded as a slab of the cross-polytope, but an exact, dimension-uniform count needs additional antipodal-pair split counting. The general prism-to-slab equivalence alone neither fixes the maximum nor enumerates the feasible vertex counts.

evidence: De Loera et al. (arXiv:2412.12419) Table 1 tabulates hypercube vertex sequences up to dimension seven; its rows are not cross-polytope prisms.
The dimension-three generic missing value 7 and the formulas for all dimensions are explicit here; no identical table was identified in the inspected literature.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Hypercube slice tables and general combinatorial enumeration are not exact entries for the cross-polytope prism. Absence from inspected tables alone is not treated as proof of priority.

originality.rationale: The quantified sharp bound, complete explicit generic vertex-number spectrum, realizability in all dimensions, and cut-gap are not statements in the primary material actually inspected. The 2026 prism-to-slab equivalence is a relevant general structural reduction, but contains no cross-polytope-specific sharp formula or integer-spectrum computation; the 2024 all-polytope upper bound is quantitatively weaker on this family. Index and own-claim comparisons found no statement implying the result. This is best-knowledge originality, not a universal priority certificate.
residual_risks: An older unindexed paper or a special case of a general slab-count formula may contain the same bound or spectrum under different terminology.
Only bibliographic and chapter information for Ziegler’s 1994 book was available, not full-text review.
The 2026 paper has a closely relevant general prism-to-slab result; extracting stronger consequences from other, less directly relevant portions could change the priority assessment.
Only self-review was performed; no external independent validation.

value.rationale: The complete generic spectrum of section vertices is a structural classification in all dimensions for a canonical nonsimple Hanner-polytope family, with a sharp vertex maximum and unique maximizing sign-count signature. It proves nontrivial gaps, including the missing count 7 in the four-dimensional octahedral prism; the strict gap to the graph MAXCUT quantifies genuinely geometric constraints beyond combinatorial edge cuts. Both the family and the invariant are natural in polytope slicing; the result is more than a routine special-case substitution.
